extra.message: searchRoutesByCriteria builds a WHERE clause by interpolating user-controlled field, operator, and value directly into sql.raw(`${entry.field} ${entry.operator} '${entry.value}'`). The criteria array is taken verbatim from the POST /api/routes/search body with only requireAuth (any authenticated user). This allows arbitrary SQL injection.

searchJobsBySavedFilter concatenates the raw filterExpression into a SQL string and executes it via db.execute(sql.raw(query)). filterExpression comes directly from the /api/reports/jobs/saved-filter query parameter with no validation, allowing full SQL injection.

findIncidentsMatchingSavedView interpolates attacker-controlled field, operator, and value into raw SQL via sql.raw(`${field} ${rawSqlOperator[op] ?? op} '${opValue}'`) and sql.raw(`${field} = '${value}'`). Criteria come from the POST /api/incidents/queue/saved-view body, allowing SQL injection.

convertRouteManifestForExport interpolates the user-controlled reportType (from the /api/export/routes/convert/:reportType URL path parameter, unvalidated) into a shell command `cat ... | csvformat -${reportType}` and runs it via spawn('sh', ['-c', command]). This permits OS command injection.

renderShippingLabel passes user-controlled labelFormat (from the POST /api/jobs/:id/shipping-label body, only sliced to 10 chars) directly into execSync(`labelconv --job ${jobPublicId} --format ${labelFormat}`), allowing OS command injection.

computeCustomAccessorialCharge evaluates attacker-controlled formulaExpression by building a function via new Function(...paramNames, `return (${formulaExpression});`). formulaExpression comes from the POST /api/carriers/rate-formulas/preview body, enabling arbitrary JavaScript execution (remote code execution).

resolveExternalEntities parses <!ENTITY ... SYSTEM "..."> declarations out of attacker-supplied XML and resolves them with fs.readFile (stripping a file:// prefix), then substitutes the file contents into the document. The /api/routes/:id/carrier-acknowledgment endpoint passes raw xmlContent here, allowing arbitrary file read / XXE.

archiveRouteManifest joins attacker-controlled archiveLabel (from the /api/routes/:id/manifest.csv/archive/:archiveLabel path parameter) into a filesystem path without basename/sanitization: path.join(routeArchiveDir, `${archiveLabel}.csv`). A traversal label such as ../../... writes files outside the archive directory.

reopenArchivedRouteManifest reads path.join(routeArchiveDir, `${archiveLabel}.csv`) where archiveLabel comes from the /api/route-manifests/:label/archived path parameter with no basename/sanitization, allowing arbitrary file read via path traversal.

storeCarrierBrandingAsset uses the upload's original filename (upload.filename, attacker-controlled via multipart) directly in path.join(carrierAssetsDir, originalFileName), allowing path traversal to write arbitrary files (including into the served public/ directory), without any mime-type or name validation.

renderStatusWidgetEmbed injects publicId, status, and partnerLabel into an inline <script> block without HTML/JS escaping. These values come from the unauthenticated /api/public/status-widget/:publicId/:partnerLabel/embed path parameters, enabling reflected cross-site scripting.

resumeCarrierOnboardingFlow redirects to the returnTo value taken directly from the onboarding_return_to cookie with no allowlist validation (reply.redirect(returnTo)). The /api/onboarding/continue endpoint uses this, enabling open redirect.

syncCustomerManifestFeed fetches an arbitrary URL taken from the preferred_manifest_source cookie with no URL/host validation (fetch(feedUrl)). The POST /api/customers/:id/manifest-feed/sync endpoint requires only authentication, allowing server-side request forgery against internal network resources.

updateWorkerPreferences spreads the entire request body into db.update(users).set({ ...updates }) with no field allowlist. A field_worker can PATCH /api/workers/:id/preferences for their own id and set arbitrary user columns (e.g. role: 'ops_admin'), escalating their own privileges.

recordPayoutRegistrationOutcome logs the full submission object (including bankAccountNumber and bankRoutingNumber) at warn level. The POST /api/workers/:id/payout-method endpoint passes the request body here, exposing sensitive banking data in application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The environment config falls back to hardcoded secrets when variables are unset: database URL with credentials (dispatch:dispatch), a predictable JWT secret ('local-dev-only-change-me-field-dispatch'), a handoff signing secret, and a carrier billing API key. If deployed without these env vars, JWT tokens can be forged and credentials are public.

lookupCustomsManifestByPartnerTenant interpolates unescaped tenantId and documentType (from the x-partner-tenant header and documentType query parameter) into an XPath expression. A value containing "' or '" bypasses the intended tenant/document scoping and returns all manifest records (information disclosure).

createAccountInviteLink generates the invite code using Math.random() (predictable PRNG), unlike the verified variant which uses crypto.randomBytes. Predictable invite tokens can be guessed to gain unauthorized access to a customer portal.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator

extra.message: searchFacilityStaffDirectory interpolates the searchTerm (from the x-search-term header) unescaped into an LDAP-style filter (&(objectClass=person)(cn=*${searchTerm}*)). Unlike verifyFacilityGroupMembership (which uses escapeDirectoryFilterValue), no escaping is applied, permitting LDAP filter injection.
